content:
Facts: Plaintiff-cousins challenged 2021 holographic will appointing minor sole heir claiming date non-autograph; asserted 2018 public will naming them heirs should govern; argued close-relationship with deceased versus broken-relationship between deceased and minor's parents; defendant contested claiming will entirely authentic, compatible with comparative-writings, relationship-deterioration with plaintiffs; court-appointed expert confirmed text/signature/date written same-hand, entirely-holographic.
Legal Framework: Articles 602, 606 Italian Civil Code (holographic validity requirements; nullity); established case law on progressive will-drafting (Cass. 2074/1985); burden-proof for negative-authenticity assessment (Cass. SU 12307/2015, Cass. 24835/2022).
Interpretive Issues: Burden-proof allocation for holographic-will negative-authenticity assessment; probative-weight of court-appointed expert versus party-consultant findings; admissibility of expert-renewal requests; whether date added later-time with different writing-instrument/physical-condition invalidates holographic-will; progressive-will-drafting validity when date affixed subsequent to text/signature.
Principles Applied: Party contesting holographic-will authenticity must file negative-origin-assessment claim; burden-proof lies with contesting-party per general negative-assessment principles. Holographic-will possesses intrinsic demonstrative-force differentiating from ordinary-documents; contesting-party raises quaestio-inexistentiae removing succession-title through falsity-recognition. Plaintiff burden-proof unmet; handwriting-analysis showed will holographic: text/bottom-signature/date written same-hand. Expert-conclusions confirmed criminal-proceedings expert-report establishing will holographic, entirely deceased-hand-written. Expert-conclusions convincing given: (a) logical-process/argumentation supporting findings; (b) responses to plaintiff-consultant observations. Detailed graphic-investigation expressing specific-technical expertise, accuracy/diligence; analysis/evaluation divided two-phases: (1) independent will-investigation identifying particularities (general-analysis highlighting main-characteristics, detailed-analysis evaluating handwriting-particularities/morphodynamic letter-structure); (2) will-analysis together comparative-documents using same-examination modus-operandi. Expert exhaustively responded plaintiff-consultant observations: date-description completeness (alleged-anomalous extrinsic-marks explained as marker-pen ink-blurring from pen-movement); dating examination-thoroughness (labored-strokes attributable advanced graphomotor-ageing stage versus text/signature time; dating done later-date, probably-years after will-writing/signature, figures reflecting different-physical-condition versus writing/signing time); graphic-similarities identified comparative-text internal-movements. Further digit-comparison with comparative-writings addressing technical-observations. Graphomotor-skill-degree response: alleged-2021-signature instability contradicted; 2016/2018 signatures show no greater-instability/angularity/softness-reduction/disconnections; 2021 power-attorney signature shows no neurological-ageing signs; upward-baseline trend linked extrinsic-factors (sheet-positioning) and intrinsic-factors (hand-posture relative writer-posture), not neurodegenerative-problems. Neurodegenerative-phenomena begin 2022 comparative-document showing graphomotor-difficulties/tremors. Expert re-analyzed all-graphic material responding each-critical note confirming: text/bottom-signature/date written same-hand; will holographic. Trial-judge not required ordering new-expert opinion even upon explicit-party request; renewal falls discretionary-powers; express-ruling unnecessary. Will-validity unaffected by: date-written different-instrument (synthetic-tipped marker versus text/signature), added later-date probably-years after writing/signing, figures reflecting different-physical-condition. No-rule establishes holographic-will must be drafted/signed single-timeframe; progressively-draftable; valid when testator uses own previously-handwritten notes adding date/signature/intention-revealing expressions later-date. Deceased likely undecided long-time regarding heir-appointment (evidenced four-different wills); intended affixing date when testamentary-wishes consolidated regarding specific-person devolution. Plausible deceased physical-condition partly-different at dating-time versus drafting/signing time; circumstance insufficient raising mental-capacity doubts existing at will-drafting time when must exist; no senile-decline signs shown. Holographic-will entirely deceased-written; prevails as subsequent to 2018 public-will.
